svg.title: Graphic 11.2 — Why the Cliff Alarm Always Fires Too Late
svg.desc: A real Zumo 32U4 is shown from the side at a table edge and from above approaching a gap. The lower half compares the 180 millisecond warning time with the 400 millisecond wait time and explains why no cliff threshold can work.
svg.text: GRAPHIC 11.2 — Why the Cliff Alarm Can Never Fire
The void reads BLACK — the same number the line reads.
…and the robot calls that A LINE.
…and the robot calls that A LINE too.
One number, two worlds — the tape it must follow and the drop it must avoid.
There is no threshold that works. Not a badly chosen one — there is NO SUCH NUMBER.
Going slower will not help. Nor will a boom. Reflectance cannot measure distance.
